title: Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 1.2.4: Ensure 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to '15 or more minute(s)'

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

steps.name: Check if the Account Lockout Policy is applied via the Default Domain Policy GPO
steps.function: 1. Check if the Account Lockout Policy is applied via the Default Domain Policy GPO using command: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String -Pattern 'LockoutDuration|LockoutObservationWindow|LockoutThreshold'`. Expected result: The Default Domain Policy GPO contains the Account Lockout Policy settings (LockoutDuration, LockoutObservationWindow, LockoutThreshold).

steps.name: Check the 'Reset account lockout counter after' value
steps.function: 2. Check the 'Reset account lockout counter after' value using command: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String -Pattern 'LockoutObservationWindow'`. Expected result: LockoutObservationWindow value is set to 15 or more minutes (900 or more seconds).

steps.name: Check that the 'Reset account lockout counter after' value is less than or equal to the 'Account lockout duration' value
steps.function: 3. Check that the 'Reset account lockout counter after' value is less than or equal to the 'Account lockout duration' value using command: `Get-GPO -Name 'Default Domain Policy' | Get-GPOReport -ReportType Xml | Select-String -Pattern 'LockoutDuration|LockoutObservationWindow'`. Expected result: LockoutObservationWindow (reset counter) value is less than or equal to LockoutDuration value.

steps.name: Check the overall compliance status
steps.function: 4. Check the overall compliance status. Expected result: PASS if the Account Lockout Policy is applied via Default Domain Policy GPO and 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to 15 or more minutes and is less than or equal to the Account lockout duration; SKIP if the Account Lockout Policy is not applied via the Default Domain Policy GPO; FAIL if the policy is applied but 'Reset account lockout counter after' is set to less than 15 minutes or exceeds the Account lockout duration.

steps.name: Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance…
steps.function: 5. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

steps.function:
6. Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg with EXACTLY this format:
AUDIT REPORT — CIS 1.2.4
Reference: CIS Benchmark checkpoint 1.2.4
Then for each requirement: REQUIREMENT NN - {{ req_NN }}:
  With fields: Task, Command, Exit code, Data, Status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR), Details.
End with OVERALL COMPLIANCE: section containing Result: {{{ cis_result }}}

steps.function: Output the overall compliance status to the caller.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
